title: Owlcrate — midnight logistics scratchpad
content:
Quick context:
- Night window (2300-0700) glaze: low traffic but high variance from batch jobs kicking at 00:15 UTC. Keep an eye on 00:10-00:30 for prefix-cache churn.
- Primary focus tonight: keep 95th p50 latency under night-slo (200ms) for hosted API; degrade gracefully to dedicated-fallback if GPU pool saturates.
- Recent change: small routing tweak merged in feature/route-fallback (PR 4897) — watch for an increase in model-fallback events.

Active items / state of health:
1) No P0s open at handoff.
2) Ongoing: INC-8421 (client-side tokenization mismatch) — in triage, assigned to Nina. Temporary mitigation applied (force model variant v2b for client xyz). Monitor error-rate in /errors?service=tokenizer; check spikes >0.5% over 5m.
3) High kv-cache miss rate observed at 00:17 UTC last night for serving-runtime shard-7. Cause suspected: nightly artifact redeploy of v3.2 quantized weights. We rolled back to v3.1-cached image; eviction rate normalized.

Immediate triage checklist (what I did / what you should check):
- Dashboards: open SLO dashboard -> hosts: serving-runtime / latency / kv-cache-hit-rate. Time range: last 2h and last 24h.
- If kv-cache hit-rate < 85% for >10m: run quick-query on shard node: ssh gpu-shard-07 -> sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime | tail -n 200 -> look for KVCacheEvict/Restart logs.
- Command: kubectl -n rw get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o wide | grep shard-7 -> if pod restarts > 3, escalate to infra (Ethan).
- Health endpoint: curl -sS https://internal-health/serving-runtime/shard-7/health | jq '.cache.hitrate, .uptime'

Temporary fixes we use frequently (notes):
- Force fallback to non-quantized model (cheap but higher latency) for specific customer routes: POST /admin/route-fallback {"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gptx-1-std"} (requires admin token). Use only if error-rate >= 1% and auto-fallback fails.
- Restart sequence for stuck GPU worker: systemctl restart serving-runtime-worker && sleep 12 && journalctl -u serving-runtime-worker -n 100. If restart loops, tag with node label broken=gpu and move traffic via smart-routing to other shards.

Escalation path (fast):
- If request latency p95 > 1s for >5m AND error-rate >2%: page SRE lead (Ethan Brooks) -> Slack #oncall-page -> call escalation number in INC-8421.
- If multiple shards evict KV within 15m: this is likely model artifact regression; page infra on-call and post the output of: kubectl -n infra logs deployment/model-deployer-main --since=30m | grep "artifact"

Known quirks / gotchas to remember (from prior nights):
- Redis cache TTL drift: we still see occasional drift after daylight-savers time changes in the lab — manual TTL reset needed: redis-cli -h cache-prod GETSET prefix-expire 3600.
- Client xyz will mis-handle 0-token responses and retry aggressively; watch for client_xyz retries metric -> set temporary per-route rate-limit if needed.
- Private deployments: some customer VPCs block health ping, so Service Monitor shows node DOWN while runtime is fine. Validate by SSH to bastion and running local healthcheck.

Owner-specific notes (Maya):
- I validated the routing tweak rollback in canary at 01:40 UTC; left a soft note in PR 4897. If you see model-fallback increase, confirm canary status: /admin/canaries -> see canary=route-fallback-2026-03-12.
- Left a TODO for Product: ask for stronger client-side backoff on tokenizer mismatch (ticket: INC-8421)

Post-shift tasks for next oncall (handoff):
- Summarize any kv-cache evictions (nodes and timestamps) and paste into CONFLUENCE-serve-runtime-ops as a short table.
- If we used the force fallback (admin API), include exact payload and timestamp.
- Verify rollback PRs: feature/route-fallback revert status.

Cheat sheet commands (copy-paste):
- Check stash of serving pods: kubectl -n rw get pods -l app=serving-runtime -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount --no-headers
- Quick tail logs for shard-7: kubectl -n rw logs deployment/serving-runtime-shard-7 -c runtime --tail=200 | grep -i "evict\|cache\|error"
- Health check endpoint: curl -fS https://internal-health/serving-runtime/shard-7/metrics | grep kv_cache_hit_rate

Loose ends / items to follow up:
- Nina: resolution plan for INC-8421 and client deploy timeline.
- Infra: confirm if nightly job that pulled new quantized artifact is backfilled (ticket INF-1102).
- Product: get confirmation on per-route temporary rate-limit window for client_xyz.

Notes to self (quick):
- If restart fixed things, annotate pod with annotation restart.reason=night-ops to help metric grouping.
- Keep a short blurb in the shift chat with: "No P0s. Applied temporary fallback to client xyz. Observed kv-cache evictions on shard-7 at 00:17, rolled back artifact. Monitoring normal."

Signoff:
- I will leave my phone on (Maya) until 01:00 UTC in case INC-8421 needs live triage. Passing to Ethan for second half of night.

End of scratchpad.
